layers.note: A herb of prairies, oak woodland, clearings and open forest edges.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,500 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

shade_tolerance.note: Grows in sun or light shade.

coldest_c.note: Across its range (see the provenance note), coldest-month means from about −2 °C, gone by −6 °C, up to about 12 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Hard frost harms it: lows to about −18 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −26 °C.

warmest_c.note: Warm, dry summers: warmest-month means from about 15.5 to 27 °C, gone below 13 °C and above 30.5 °C.

degree_days_0.note: A long warm season: about 3,100 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 2,400.

degree_days_5.note: About 1,600 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 1,100: it stays in warm lowlands and on the lower slopes.

moisture_index.note: Summer drought borne: a moisture index from about 0.32 (gone by 0.2), dry savanna and prairie climates included.

summer_rain.note: A Mediterranean-type climate: its range lies where at most about 0.2 of the year's precipitation falls in summer, gone by 0.35.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Oregon iris grows in meadows and open woods of western Washington and Oregon (the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
